questions.title: Two Sum Indexes
questions.prompt: Return the indexes of two different numbers that add up to a target. Return an empty list if no pair exists.
constraints: Each index can be used once.
hints: Store values you have seen with their index.
For each number, compute target minus number.
Check whether the complement was seen earlier.

visualizer.title: Two Sum: remember what you have seen
visualizer.caption: Watch a hash map store earlier values so the complement lookup is quick.

questions.title: Balanced Brackets
questions.prompt: Return true if brackets (), [], and {} are correctly balanced and nested.
hints: Use a stack for opening brackets.
When you see a closing bracket, compare it with the stack top.
At the end, the stack should be empty.

visualizer.title: Balanced Brackets: match the newest opener
visualizer.caption: Watch opening brackets go on the stack and closing brackets remove the matching top.

questions.title: Longest Unique Window
questions.prompt: Return the length of the longest substring with no repeated characters.
constraints: Input length can be up to 10000.
hints: Keep a window with left and right indexes.
Remember the most recent index of each character.
Move the left side past duplicates.

questions.title: Group Anagrams
questions.prompt: Group words that are anagrams of each other. Return groups in any order.
hints: Anagrams share the same sorted letters.
Use the sorted word as a key.
Append each word to its key's group.

questions.title: Merge Sorted Lists
questions.prompt: Given two integer lists that are already sorted in ascending order, return one new sorted list containing every value from both lists.
hints: Use one pointer for each list.
Append the smaller current value.
Append any leftovers after one list ends.

questions.title: Course Prerequisite Chain
questions.prompt: Given pairs [course, prerequisite], return true if a target course eventually depends on a given prerequisite.
constraints: Pairs form a directed dependency graph.
hints: Create a lookup where each course points to the courses it needs first.
Start from the target course and follow its prerequisites one step at a time.
Return true as soon as the prerequisite you are looking for appears.

visualizer.title: Prerequisites: follow graph links
visualizer.caption: Watch the search move from a course to the classes it depends on.

questions.title: Top K Frequent
questions.prompt: Return the k most frequent values in a list. If frequencies tie, any order is acceptable.
hints: Count each value first.
Sort or bucket by frequency.
Return the first k values.

questions.title: Matrix Row Sums
questions.prompt: Return a list containing the sum of each row in a matrix.
hints: Loop through each row.
Sum values in that row.
Append the row sum to the result.

questions.title: Rotate List Right
questions.prompt: Given a list and a number k, move each item k places to the right and wrap items from the end back to the front.
constraints: k may be larger than the list length.
hints: Use k modulo length.
Split the list at length - k.
Put the ending slice before the starting slice.

questions.title: First Missing Positive Small
questions.prompt: Return the smallest positive integer that does not appear in the list.
constraints: A set-based solution is fine for this version.
hints: Put all values in a set.
Start checking from 1.
Return the first positive number not in the set.

questions.title: Compress Runs
questions.prompt: Compress repeated adjacent characters as character plus count. Single characters still include count 1.
hints: Track the current character and count.
When the character changes, append the completed run.
Do not forget the final run.

questions.title: Valid Study Schedule
questions.prompt: Given meeting intervals [start, end], return false if any intervals overlap, otherwise true.
constraints: End time equal to next start time is allowed.
hints: Sort intervals by start time.
Track the largest end time seen so far as you scan.
If a start time is less than that running largest end, there is overlap.

questions.title: Binary Search Insert Position
questions.prompt: Given a sorted list and target, return the index where the target is found or should be inserted.
hints: Use left and right bounds.
Move toward the first value greater than or equal to target.
When the loop ends, left is the insertion index.

visualizer.title: Binary Search: shrink toward the insert spot
visualizer.caption: Watch left, mid, and right move until the insert position is clear.

questions.title: Count Islands
questions.prompt: Given a grid of 1s and 0s, count connected groups of 1s using up, down, left, and right neighbors.
hints: Scan the grid one cell at a time looking for a 1 that has not been handled yet.
When you find one, explore its up, down, left, and right neighbors to find the whole island.
Mark every cell in that island before you continue scanning, then add 1 to the island count.

questions.title: Min Stack Operations
questions.prompt: Process stack commands push x, pop, top, and min. Return outputs for top and min commands.
constraints: Commands are valid for this version.
hints: Use a normal stack for values.
Use a second stack for current minimums.
Update the minimum stack on push and pop.

visualizer.title: Min Stack: stack operations first
visualizer.caption: Watch push, peek, and pop before adding the second minimum stack idea.

questions.title: Normalize Email List
questions.prompt: Lowercase and trim each email, remove duplicates, and return the cleaned list in first-seen order.
constraints: Emails are strings; do not validate domain.
hints: Trim whitespace and lowercase first.
Use a set for cleaned emails already used.
Append only first occurrences.

questions.title: Prefix Search
questions.prompt: Return all words that start with a given prefix, preserving input order.
hints: Loop over words.
Use a starts-with check.
Collect matches in order.

questions.title: Window Average
questions.prompt: Return averages for every contiguous window of size k in a list of numbers.
hints: Compute the first window sum.
Slide by subtracting the outgoing value and adding the incoming value.
Divide each window sum by k.

visualizer.title: Window Average: slide one spot at a time
visualizer.caption: Watch the outgoing value leave, the incoming value enter, and the sum update.

questions.title: Nested List Depth Sum
questions.prompt: Given nested integers, return the sum of each integer multiplied by its depth. Top-level depth is 1.
constraints: Input is a nested list of integers.
hints: Write a helper with value and depth.
If the value is an integer, return value times depth.
If it is a list, recurse into each item with depth + 1.

visualizer.title: Nested Depth Sum: call smaller pieces
visualizer.caption: Watch recursive calls go deeper before answers come back up.

questions.title: Most Recent Unique
questions.prompt: Given event names in chronological order, return the most recent event that appears exactly once. Return null if none exist.
hints: Count event frequencies.
Scan from the end of the list.
Return the first event whose count is one.

questions.title: Pair Sum Sorted
questions.prompt: Given a sorted list of integers, return true if two different values add up to the target.
constraints: The input list is sorted ascending.
hints: Because the list is sorted, the smallest value is on the left and the largest is on the right.
Add those two values and compare the sum to the target.
If the sum is too small, move left forward; if it is too large, move right backward.

visualizer.title: Pair Sum Sorted: move the pointer that helps
visualizer.caption: Watch the left and right pointers use sorted order to find the target.

questions.title: Binary Search Exact
questions.prompt: Given a sorted list and a target, return the target's index or -1 if it is not present.
hints: Keep two bounds: left starts at the first index and right starts at the last index.
Check the middle index between left and right.
If the middle value is not the target, move the bound that lets you ignore the impossible half.

visualizer.title: Binary Search Exact: check the middle
visualizer.caption: Watch each comparison remove half of the remaining search range.

questions.title: Help Desk Queue
questions.prompt: Process help desk commands. 'join name' adds a student to the back. 'serve' removes the front student and records their name. If the queue is empty, record 'none'.
hints: A queue means first student in, first student served.
For a join command, put the name at the back of the waiting list.
For a serve command, record the front name; if nobody is waiting, record 'none'.

visualizer.title: Help Desk Queue: first student served first
visualizer.caption: Watch names join at the back and leave from the front.

questions.title: Recursive Digit Sum
questions.prompt: Return the sum of the digits of a non-negative integer using a recursive idea.
hints: A recursive solution needs a stopping case first: a one-digit number returns itself.
Use n % 10 to get the last digit.
Add that digit to the answer for the smaller number n // 10.

visualizer.title: Recursive Digit Sum: base case and return path
visualizer.caption: Watch 407 become smaller calls, then add answers while returning.

questions.title: Range Sum Queries
questions.prompt: Given a list of numbers and queries [left, right], return the sum inside each inclusive range.
hints: Make a running-total list where prefix[i] stores the sum before index i.
For a query from left to right, subtract the total before left from the total after right.
That formula is prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left].

questions.title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
questions.prompt: Given intervals [start, end], merge overlapping intervals and return the merged list sorted by start.
constraints: Touching intervals like [1,2] and [2,3] should merge.
hints: Sort the intervals by start time so overlaps are next to each other.
Keep a merged list and compare each new interval with the last interval in that list.
If the new start is before or equal to the last end, extend the last end; otherwise add a new interval.

questions.title: Maximum Window Sum
questions.prompt: Return the largest sum of any contiguous window of size k.
hints: First add the first k numbers; that is your first window sum.
Move the window one step by subtracting the number that left and adding the number that entered.
After each move, update the best sum if the new window is larger.

visualizer.title: Maximum Window Sum: keep a running total
visualizer.caption: Watch the sum change by subtracting one value and adding one value.

questions.title: Campus Stop Reachable
questions.prompt: Given shuttle connections between campus stops, return true if a student can travel from the start stop to the target stop by following one or more connections.
constraints: Connections are directed for this practice version.
hints: Build a graph where each stop points to the stops it can reach next.
Use a stack or queue starting from the start stop.
Mark stops as visited so a loop in the shuttle route does not trap your search.

visualizer.title: Campus Stop Reachable: search connected stops
visualizer.caption: Watch a graph search move from one shuttle stop to the next.

questions.title: Top Priority Assignments
questions.prompt: Given assignment names and priority scores, return the k assignment names with the highest priority. If priorities tie, return the tied names in alphabetical order.
hints: Pair each name with its priority first.
Sort by priority from high to low, and by name from A to Z for ties.
Return only the first k names from that ordered list.

questions.title: Club Membership Groups
questions.prompt: Given n students and pairs of students in the same club network, return how many separate club groups exist after all memberships are connected.
constraints: A pair means both students belong to the same connected group.
hints: Start with every student in their own group.
For each pair, connect the two groups if they are not already connected.
Count how many unique group leaders remain after all pairs are processed.

questions.title: Prefix Match Count
questions.prompt: Given a word list and a prefix, return how many words start with that prefix. An empty prefix matches every word.
constraints: An empty prefix returns the number of words.
hints: A trie can answer this quickly, but a direct scan is fine here.
Check each word with a starts-with comparison.
Increase the count only when the word begins with the prefix.

questions.title: Linked List Middle Value
questions.prompt: A linked list is represented by values, nextIndexes, and a head index. Return the middle node value. When there are two middle nodes, return the second one. Return -1 for an empty list.
hints: Follow the list into an ordered list of values first.
The second middle is at index length // 2.
Return -1 when head is -1.

visualizer.title: Middle Value: count positions
visualizer.caption: Watch the traversal create an ordered view before choosing the middle.

questions.title: Linked List Has Cycle
questions.prompt: A linked list is represented by nextIndexes and a head index. Return true if following next indexes eventually repeats an index, otherwise false.
constraints: Head may be -1 for an empty list.
hints: Keep a set of indexes already visited.
If the current index appears again, there is a cycle.
If you reach -1, the list ends with no cycle.

visualizer.title: Cycle Check: remember visited nodes
visualizer.caption: Watch traversal stop when it sees the same index twice.

questions.title: Daily Temperature Waits
questions.prompt: Given daily temperatures, return how many days each day must wait until a warmer temperature. Use 0 when no warmer future day exists.
constraints: Return one wait count for every input day.
hints: Keep indexes for days still waiting for a warmer temperature.
When today is warmer than the stack top day, fill that earlier answer.
Push today's index after resolving colder previous days.

visualizer.title: Temperature Waits: unresolved days stack
visualizer.caption: Watch colder days wait on the stack until a warmer day resolves them.

questions.title: Recent Queue Counts
questions.prompt: Given non-decreasing request times and a window size, return how many requests are still inside the rolling window after each new request arrives. A request stays while currentTime - oldTime is less than or equal to window.
hints: Use a queue of recent request times.
Add the current time to the back.
Remove times from the front while they are older than the allowed window.

visualizer.title: Recent Requests: discard old front items
visualizer.caption: Watch old timestamps leave from the front as the window moves.

questions.title: First Bad Version
questions.prompt: Versions are stored as a sorted list of 0s and 1s, where 0 means good and 1 means bad. Return the first bad index, or -1 if there is no bad version.
constraints: The list may contain all good or all bad versions.
hints: This is a boundary search.
If the middle is bad, the first bad version is at mid or to the left.
If the middle is good, search to the right.

visualizer.title: First Bad: shrink to the boundary
visualizer.caption: Watch binary search keep the earliest possible bad version.

questions.title: Reverse Linked List Values
questions.prompt: A linked list is represented by values, nextIndexes, and a head index. Return the node values in reverse traversal order without changing the input arrays.
hints: Traverse from head to collect values in normal order.
Reverse the collected values at the end.
An empty list returns an empty result.

visualizer.title: Reverse Values: collect then reverse
visualizer.caption: Watch normal traversal produce values that are reversed afterward.

questions.title: Parking Ticket Total
questions.prompt: Return the campus parking ticket total for a student's car based on the day, hour, parked minutes, and permit status.
constraints: day is one of Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, or Sunday.
Weekday parking is free before 7:00 and at or after 19:00.
Wednesday visitor fair parking is free during hours 12 and 13.
Ticketed parking starts with a 20 dollar base fee.
Add 10 dollars when minutesParked is greater than 120.
Add 15 dollars when the student has no permit during busy hours 9 through 16.
On Friday at or after 15:00, do not add the no-permit busy-hour fee.
hints: Handle the free parking cases first so you can return 0 early.
After free parking is ruled out, begin with the 20 dollar base ticket.
Add the long-parking fee and no-permit busy-hour fee only when their conditions apply.

questions.title: Reverse Only Letters
questions.prompt: Reverse only the letters in a string while keeping numbers, spaces, and punctuation in their original positions.
constraints: Non-letter characters stay at the same index.
hints: Use one pointer from the left and one from the right.
Move a pointer past characters that are not letters.
When both pointers are on letters, swap them and move both inward.

visualizer.title: Reverse Letters: skip punctuation
visualizer.caption: Watch pointers skip fixed characters and swap only letters.

questions.title: Minimum Study Window
questions.prompt: Return the length of the shortest contiguous group of study sessions whose total minutes is at least the target. Return 0 if no group can reach the target.
constraints: Return 0 when no contiguous window reaches target.
hints: Grow the right side until the window total reaches the target.
Once the window is large enough, record its length.
Shrink from the left while the total still meets the target.

visualizer.title: Minimum Window: grow then shrink
visualizer.caption: Watch a window expand to reach the target, then shrink to improve the answer.

questions.title: Recursive Power
questions.prompt: Return base raised to exponent using a recursive idea. The exponent is non-negative.
constraints: Use integer multiplication; no floating-point results are needed.
hints: The stopping case is exponent == 0.
For the recursive step, multiply base by the answer for exponent - 1.
Each call should make the exponent smaller so the recursion eventually stops.

visualizer.title: Power: repeated smaller calls
visualizer.caption: Watch exponent shrink until the base case, then multiply while returning.

questions.title: Tree Leaf Count
questions.prompt: A binary tree is stored as a level-order list where -1 means missing. Return how many real nodes are leaves.
constraints: Use -1 only as the missing-node marker.
A leaf is a real node with no real left or right child.
hints: For an index i, children are at 2*i+1 and 2*i+2.
A missing or out-of-range child does not count as real.
Count the node when both children are missing.

visualizer.title: Leaf Count: check children
visualizer.caption: Watch each real node decide whether it has real children.

questions.title: Tree Contains Value
questions.prompt: A binary tree is stored as a level-order list where -1 means missing. Return true if the target value appears in a real node.
constraints: Use -1 only as the missing-node marker.
Target may be negative, but -1 in the tree still means missing.
Return false for an empty tree.
hints: Scan the level-order list.
Ignore -1 markers because they are missing nodes.
Return true as soon as a real node equals target.

visualizer.title: Tree Search: scan real nodes
visualizer.caption: Watch level-order values get checked against the target.

questions.title: Prefix Balance Index
questions.prompt: Given daily study minutes, return the first index where the total before that day equals the total after that day. Return -1 if no balance point exists.
constraints: The current index value is not included in either side.
hints: Find the total sum first.
Keep a running left sum as you scan.
The right sum is total - left sum - current value.

questions.title: Matrix Diagonal Sum
questions.prompt: Given a square campus seating grid, return the sum of both diagonals without counting the center seat twice.
constraints: For odd sizes, count the center cell once.
hints: The main diagonal uses row i and column i.
The other diagonal uses row i and column n - 1 - i.
When both columns are the same, add that cell only once.

questions.title: Different Bit Count
questions.prompt: Two lab devices send integer status codes. Return how many binary bit positions are different between the two codes.
constraints: a and b are non-negative integers.
Only positions where one code has 1 and the other has 0 count.
A direct loop over the xor value is fine.
hints: XOR marks positions where the bits differ.
Count the 1 bits in a xor b.
Shift or divide until no differing bits remain.

questions.title: Matrix Border Sum
questions.prompt: Given a rectangular garden grid, return the sum of the values on the outside border.
constraints: Single-row and single-column matrices should not double-count cells.
hints: A cell is on the border if it is in the first row, last row, first column, or last column.
Scan every cell once and add only border cells.
Return 0 for an empty matrix.

questions.title: Longest Common Prefix
questions.prompt: Given a list of course topic words, return the longest prefix shared by every word. Return an empty string if there is no shared prefix.
constraints: The word list may be empty.
A direct character scan is acceptable before building a trie.
hints: Start with the first word as the possible prefix.
Compare each later word against that prefix.
Shorten the prefix until the current word starts with it.

questions.title: Count Overlapping Intervals
questions.prompt: Given tutoring availability intervals [start, end] and a time, return how many intervals include that time.
constraints: Intervals use inclusive start and exclusive end: start <= time < end.
Return 0 when no interval contains the time.
hints: Scan each interval independently.
Check whether start is less than or equal to time.
Also check that time is less than end before counting it.

questions.title: Lowest Priority Assignment
questions.prompt: Given assignment names and priority scores, return the name with the lowest priority score. If scores tie, return the alphabetically first tied name.
constraints: names and priorities have the same length.
The input has at least one assignment.
hints: Pair each assignment name with its priority.
Track the smallest priority seen so far.
For a tie, compare the assignment names alphabetically.

questions.title: Same Club Group
questions.prompt: Given n students, same-club pairs, and two student IDs, return true if those two students end up in the same connected club group.
constraints: A student is always in the same group as themselves.
hints: Start each student in their own group.
Connect the groups for every pair.
After all pairs, compare the group leader for a and b.

questions.title: Study Plan Ways
questions.prompt: A student can finish a study plan by doing 1 day or 2 days of work at a time. Return how many different schedules can finish exactly days days.
constraints: There is 1 way to finish 0 days: choose no work blocks.
hints: The last move is either a 1-day block or a 2-day block.
Ways for days equals ways for days - 1 plus ways for days - 2.
Build from small day counts upward.

questions.title: Closest Pair Sum Sorted
questions.prompt: Given a sorted list of scores, return the two values whose sum is closest to a target total.
constraints: The input list is sorted ascending.
Return an empty list when there are fewer than two values.
If two pairs are equally close, keep the first closest pair found by the two-pointer scan.
hints: Start one pointer at the smallest value and one at the largest value.
Track the best pair and the smallest distance from target so far.
Move left forward when the sum is too small, or right backward when it is too large.

visualizer.title: Closest Pair: use sorted order
visualizer.caption: Watch the smaller or larger pointer move depending on the current sum.

questions.title: Longest Study Stretch Under Limit
questions.prompt: Given non-negative study minutes and a weekly limit, return the longest contiguous stretch whose total stays within the limit.
constraints: Return 0 when no single day fits within the limit.
hints: Grow the right side by adding the next day.
While the total is too large, shrink from the left.
After the window is valid, update the best length.

visualizer.title: Longest Valid Stretch: grow and shrink
visualizer.caption: Watch the window expand, then shrink when the total is over the limit.

questions.title: Recursive Reverse Text
questions.prompt: Return a string reversed by using the recursive idea of reversing the rest of the text before adding the first character.
constraints: Each recursive call should work on a shorter string.
hints: The base case is length 0 or 1.
For a longer string, reverse everything after the first character.
Put the first character at the end of that reversed rest.

visualizer.title: Reverse Text: rest then first
visualizer.caption: Watch each call peel off the first character and add it back on return.

questions.title: Help Session Finish Order
questions.prompt: Students wait for help. Each turn the front student uses one ticket; if they still need help, they move to the back. Return the order students finish.
constraints: names and tickets have the same length.
A student finishes when their ticket count reaches 0.
hints: Store each student's index in a queue.
On each turn, remove the front index and subtract one ticket.
If tickets remain, put that index at the back; otherwise record the name.

visualizer.title: Help Sessions: rotate unfinished students
visualizer.caption: Watch students cycle through the queue until each ticket count reaches zero.

questions.title: Last Score At Most
questions.prompt: Given sorted quiz scores and a target, return the last index whose score is less than or equal to the target.
constraints: Return -1 if every score is greater than target.
hints: This is a last-at-most boundary search.
When the middle score is allowed, remember that index and search right.
When the middle score is too large, search left.

visualizer.title: Last Score At Most: keep the rightmost match
visualizer.caption: Watch binary search move toward the last score still allowed by the target.
